$Comment:
The Enchanting tree's find techniques at both Disenchanting Tables, each read off the talent's own record (ziggfreedcommon:track_pick) and gated on it, so nobody without the talent rolls here. Each repeats a find by granting a Lootable reward naming the find's own table with Trigger Cycle, judged against this same ritual (the same piece, its level, quality and wear, and every gate the table carries), so a second roll can never pay what the first could not. One find per table is why these can name each one alone.

VOID RITE (the Seeker's Rite): from item level 30 the Void finds (Disenchant_Void, this pack's same-id copy, and Mmo_Disenchant_Void_Finds) roll a second time, and Disenchant_Essence pays no base wage on that piece. Seeker's Practice lowers the threshold a rank (25, then 20): one roll per rank, so exactly one applies.
KIT RITE (the Seeker's Rite): the disenchanter's kit (Disenchant_Kit) and the grimoire chase (DisenchantTrophy) roll a second time, and the Void finds never (both Void tables carry a Requires shutting them for this talent's holder). Seeker's Practice adds a quarter of rituals a rank (half at both ranks) on which they roll a third time.
TREASURE HUNTER (the Seeker's Trade): every find table rolls again on half of all rituals, each on its own, so each find is half again as likely; the price, a salvage return half the size, is Extensions/DisenchantingProgression.json's Recipe.Yield.Ladder.

The greater table's own extra Void chance (Mmo_Disenchant_Greater_Void) gets the same Void Rite and Treasure Hunter rolls in Mmo_Disenchant_Greater_Rites, named only there. Named by Extensions/DisenchantingProgression.json (and its greater child). Every chance and threshold is balance data; retune by shipping a same-id file from a pack loading after this one.
